questions.question: Shifting to a lower gear has an effect similar to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have a manual transmission. Shifting down to a lower gear will slow your motorcycle down.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection usually takes:

options.text: A few minutes and should be done only once a month.
A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
More than an hour and should be done by a mechanic.
More than an hour and should only be done if you have a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
questions.explanation: Do a thorough check before every ride. It should take only a few minutes.

questions.question: If you wait one hour per alcoholic drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Alcohol will not affect your skills.
Alcohol effects may still be present.
You will be safe as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol effects may still be present.
questions.explanation: Your body can eliminate about one drink per hour. However, alcohol can still build up in your system even at this rate. This buildup can still affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: Which of these clothing choices is not safe for motorcycle riding?

options.text: A jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely
Boots or shoes that cover your ankles
A baseball cap to cover your hair

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap to cover your hair
questions.explanation: To protect yourself, wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a jacket and long pants made of sturdy material, boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: A motorcycle's brake light is:

options.text: More noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less important than a car's brake lights.
Easier to see than a car's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is not as noticeable as a car's brake lights. Flash your brake light before slowing or stopping to help other drivers see that you are braking.

questions.question: Riding at night:

options.text: Is safer when you wear reflective clothing.
Is unsafe because drivers cannot see your turn signals.
Should only be done in cities.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safer when you wear reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials when riding at night to make yourself more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: When should a rider use their mirrors?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when slowing down or stopping, when stopped at intersections, when changing lanes, and when turning.

questions.question: Motorcycles have blind spots like cars. When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and check your blind spot.
Slow down so any vehicle in your blind spot can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles:

options.text: Gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
Limits your movement to one part of the lane.
Lets you rely on other drivers to see hazards.
Requires you to speed up to keep with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Space around your motorcycle gives you time and room to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: A motorcycle needs:

options.text: Pre-ride checks done only by a mechanic.

questions.correctAnswerText: More attention than a car.
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle can be more serious than on a car. Check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride.

questions.question: What color are warning signs?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What happens when you drink alcohol quickly?

options.text: The more the alcohol will accumulate in your body.
The faster the alcohol is removed from your body.
The more minimal the effects of the alcohol will be.
The more likely you will be able to evade being pulled over.

questions.correctAnswerText: The more the alcohol will accumulate in your body.
questions.explanation: When you drink quickly, alcohol builds up in your body. Never drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your chance of an accident?

options.text: Follow the vehicle in front of you as closely as possible.
Not look ahead and focus only on your controls.
Communicate your intentions to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate your intentions to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and always look ahead and around you.

questions.question: What should you wear to help other drivers see you?
questions.correctAnswerText: Brightly-colored clothes.
questions.explanation: Wear brightly-colored clothing so other drivers can see you better. This helps during both day and night riding.

questions.question: What lowers your risk of being in a crash?

options.text: Communicate your intentions to other road users.
Ride in the parts of a lane that make it difficult to be seen.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate your intentions to other road users.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to other drivers. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and constantly watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: How should a helmet fit for best protection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Fits snugly.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no obvious damage.

questions.question: What should you wear when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Not wear a jacket if it's warm out.
Always wear a jacket, even if it's warm out.
Not be concerned about long shoelaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a jacket, even if it's warm out.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket made of good material when riding, even in warm weather. This protects you and helps prevent dehydration. Always wear long pants and tuck in your shoelaces so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: What is most important about your helmet?
questions.correctAnswerText: Meets Department of Transportation guidelines.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no obvious damage.

questions.question: What do you NOT need to check before riding your motorcycle?

options.text: Trying both brake controls to ensure the brake light activates.
Ensuring that the paint is not scratched.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ensuring that the paint is not scratched.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tire pressure and condition, oil and fluid levels, and that your headlight, taillight, signal lights, and brake light all work.

questions.question: The Motorcycle Safety Foundation recommends a SEE strategy. What does "S" stand for?
questions.correctAnswerText: Search
questions.explanation: The SEE strategy stands for Search, Evaluate, and Execute. Experienced riders use this method to make safe decisions.

questions.question: When should you use a turn signal?
questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you change lanes.
questions.explanation: Use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if no one else is nearby.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get away from them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them pass.
questions.explanation: The safest way to handle a tailgater is to let them get in front of you. Change lanes when it is safe and let them pass. Speeding up may make the danger worse by encouraging them to continue tailgating at a higher speed.

questions.question: How does a three-wheeled motorcycle handle curves?

options.text: The same way as a two-wheeled motorcycle.
It should not be used on curves.
It should use the shoulder when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
questions.explanation: A three-wheeled motorcycle or one with a sidecar turns differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.question: What does long-term exposure to wind noise do?

options.text: It is safer than listening to music.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause hearing loss.
questions.explanation: Long-term wind noise from riding can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Wear proper hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: When getting ready to pass, why should you ride in the left part of your lane?

options.text: It helps you see better ahead.
It makes it harder to see ahead.
It blocks your view of the other vehicle.
It lets the other driver speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you see better ahead.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane when preparing to pass. This helps you see farther ahead and makes you more visible to drivers already in the passing lane.
